items.title: Understanding of Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain other dependents or heirs. An independent attorney can help clarify where your family stands.

items.title: Awareness of the Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing these dates can close off your right to recover.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning your family pays nothing upfront and no fee unless there is a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California after losing someone in Parlier?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a public road agency, may share fault, the deadline to act is much shorter and requires an early claim. An independent attorney can confirm the exact timeline for your situation.

items.question: Can I file a wrongful death claim if I'm not the spouse or a child of the person who died?
items.answer: California law prioritizes a spouse, domestic partner, and children as the first parties allowed to file. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing, depending on the family situation. An attorney can review your relationship to the deceased and explain whether you qualify.

items.question: Parlier crash reports show most collisions happen on Sundays in the early evening — does that affect our case?
items.answer: The timing of a crash doesn't change the legal standards for a wrongful death claim, but it can help an attorney reconstruct what happened on corridors like Manning Avenue or Academy Avenue. Public crash data adds context, though every case still turns on its own facts. This kind of detail is something an independent attorney can factor into building your claim.
